_note: Seed rows for LT01 topics T03-T06. Example IPA is hand-transcribed (see manual/MAINTENANCE.md and CLAUDE.md); review with a native speaker before publishing.

LT01T03.title: What a syllable is
LT01T03.focus: every syllable has one vowel sound at its core

LT01T03.title: Open syllables
LT01T03.focus: a syllable that ends in a vowel is open and the vowel is held clearly

LT01T03.title: Closed syllables
LT01T03.focus: a syllable that ends in a consonant is closed, and the consonant is clearly heard

LT01T03.title: Stress is free
LT01T03.focus: stress can fall on any syllable, so it must be learned with each word

LT01T03.title: Stress on the last syllable
LT01T03.focus: many words stress the final syllable

LT01T03.title: Stress on the second-last syllable
LT01T03.focus: the penultimate syllable is a common stress position

LT01T03.title: Stress on the third-last syllable
LT01T03.focus: long words often stress the antepenultimate syllable

LT01T03.title: Stress is not written
LT01T03.focus: Romanian spelling does not mark stress, so dictionaries and audio show it

LT01T03.title: Diphthongs in one syllable
LT01T03.focus: two vowels that glide together form one syllable

LT01T03.title: Hiatus splits vowels
LT01T03.focus: two neighbouring vowels that belong to separate syllables are pronounced apart

LT01T03.title: Final -ă stays clear
LT01T03.focus: the final -ă is a full vowel and is never dropped

LT01T03.title: Stress stays on the root
LT01T03.focus: stress keeps its place when a noun changes form

LT01T03.title: Stress in verb endings
LT01T03.focus: verb forms can stress the final syllable of the ending

LT01T03.title: Masculine and feminine adjectives
LT01T03.focus: the feminine form adds a syllable and moves the stress

LT01T03.title: -a and -ă endings
LT01T03.focus: the definite article -a and the ending -ă sound different

LT01T03.title: Unstressed short words
LT01T03.focus: short words such as the reflexive mă are weak and join the next word

LT01T03.title: Stress in long words
LT01T03.focus: suffixes such as -itate keep their stress pattern

LT01T03.title: Count the syllables
LT01T03.focus: clap each syllable, then mark the stressed one

LT01T03.title: Stress and vowel contrast
LT01T03.focus: the stressed and unstressed endings differ in vowel quality

LT01T03.title: Practice: stress in pairs
LT01T03.focus: say the pairs aloud and move the stress with the change of ending

LT01T04.title: Soft c before e and i
LT01T04.focus: c before e and i is pronounced like ch in church

LT01T04.title: Hard c before a, o and u
LT01T04.focus: c before a, o and u is a plain k sound

LT01T04.title: Soft g before e and i
LT01T04.focus: g before e and i is pronounced like j in jump

LT01T04.title: Hard g before a, o and u
LT01T04.focus: g before a, o and u is a plain g sound

LT01T04.title: The letters ghe and ghi
LT01T04.focus: gh before e and i keeps a hard g

LT01T04.title: The letters che and chi
LT01T04.focus: ch before e and i is a single soft sound

LT01T04.title: The sounds ș and ț
LT01T04.focus: ș is sh and ț is ts, always

LT01T04.title: Plural t becomes ț
LT01T04.focus: in many plurals the consonant t changes to ț

LT01T04.title: Plural c becomes ci
LT01T04.focus: the consonant c changes to a ch sound in some plurals

LT01T04.title: Vowel change o becomes oa
LT01T04.focus: the vowel o changes to oa in some singulars and plurals

LT01T04.title: The letters î and â
LT01T04.focus: î and â both write the sound ɨ, and î is used inside words

LT01T04.title: The letter h
LT01T04.focus: h is a clear h sound, as in hotel

LT01T04.title: The letter x
LT01T04.focus: x is pronounced gz between vowels

LT01T04.title: The letter s before e and i
LT01T04.focus: s before e and i stays a plain s sound

LT01T04.title: Practice: the soft and hard sounds
LT01T04.focus: read pairs aloud, one soft and one hard, and listen for the change

LT01T05.title: Hyphenation: split between syllables
LT01T05.focus: a word broken at the end of a line splits between syllables

LT01T05.title: Hyphenation: keep a single consonant
LT01T05.focus: a single consonant between vowels goes with the next syllable

LT01T05.title: Short forms: n-a
LT01T05.focus: nu a is often shortened to n-a in speech and writing

LT01T05.title: Clitic: mi-e
LT01T05.focus: mi-e joins the pronoun and the verb into one quick unit

LT01T05.title: Clitic: ți-e
LT01T05.focus: ți-e joins the pronoun ți and the verb e

LT01T05.title: Clitic: i-a
LT01T05.focus: i-a joins the pronoun i and the verb a

LT01T05.title: Ce-ai
LT01T05.focus: ce ai is said as one quick unit in speech

LT01T05.title: Nu-l
LT01T05.focus: nu îl is often said nu-l

LT01T05.title: Dintr-o
LT01T05.focus: the vowel o drops after the consonant in dintr-o

LT01T05.title: Într-o zi
LT01T05.focus: într-o is said with the o weak and joined to the next word

LT01T05.title: Speech rhythm: unstressed words
LT01T05.focus: short words such as în and la carry little stress and link to the next word

LT01T05.title: Practice: fast phrases
LT01T05.focus: say each phrase at normal speed and check the weak forms

LT01T06.title: Falling tone in statements
LT01T06.focus: a statement falls at its end

LT01T06.title: Rising tone in yes-no questions
LT01T06.focus: a yes-no question rises at its end

LT01T06.title: Falling tone in wh-questions
LT01T06.focus: a question with a question word falls at its end

LT01T06.title: Exclamations
LT01T06.focus: an exclamation rises high on the key word, then falls

LT01T06.title: Commands
LT01T06.focus: a command is short and falls sharply

LT01T06.title: Lists and commas
LT01T06.focus: each item in a list is a short rise, and the last item falls
LT01T06.gloss: I have bread, milk and eggs.

LT01T06.title: Dashes in dialogue
LT01T06.focus: in Romanian a dialogue line starts with a dash

LT01T06.title: Romanian quotation marks
LT01T06.focus: Romanian quotes use the low opening mark and the high closing mark

LT01T06.title: Oare in questions
LT01T06.focus: oare marks a question of doubt and keeps the rise
LT01T06.gloss: I wonder if he is coming?

LT01T06.title: Ellipsis and pauses
LT01T06.focus: three dots show a pause and a trailing voice

LT01T06.title: Parentheses and dashes
LT01T06.focus: a clause in dashes is spoken with a short pause on each side
LT01T06.gloss: He is coming, he says, tomorrow.

LT01T06.title: Rhythm of stressed syllables
LT01T06.focus: the stressed syllables set the rhythm and the unstressed ones are quick

LT01T06.title: Conditional sentences with a pause
LT01T06.focus: the first clause ends in a short rise, then the second falls

LT01T06.title: Emphasis by word order
LT01T06.focus: the emphasised word comes first and takes the strongest stress

LT01T06.title: Polite requests
LT01T06.focus: vă rog is said softly and falls, and the speaker's tone stays warm

LT01T06.title: Tag questions
LT01T06.focus: nu? at the end asks for agreement and rises

LT01T06.title: Interjections
LT01T06.focus: hei and ei are short calls with their own tone

LT01T06.title: Practice: read a sentence in chunks
LT01T06.focus: pause at each comma and let the tone rise or fall at the end of each chunk
LT01T06.gloss: Tomorrow, I am going to school.
